public.summary: Adding a backup shift also changes the original schedule. Find out why and pick a fix.
public.statement: A volunteer coordinator keeps the published schedule and a draft side by side so she can compare them. addBackupShift() should return a NEW array containing all the original shifts plus the backup shift at the end. The original schedule array must not change. After calling it, the coordinator sees the backup shift in the published schedule too. Identify the faulty line and choose a change that meets the specification.
facts: schedule is an array of shift objects; shift is one more shift object.
Arrays in JavaScript are objects; assigning one to a new variable does not copy it.

constraints.text: The original schedule array must not be modified.
The returned array contains every original shift followed by the backup shift.

answer_format.instructions: Choose the faulty line and the fix.

fields.label: Which line is the root cause?

public.explanation_prompt: Why does the original change? How would you confirm the fix leaves it untouched?

provenance.author: Reasoning Lab project team
provenance.contamination_note: Aliasing bugs are widely discussed; option d is a deliberately plausible distractor.

cases.name: original unchanged
cases.check: (() => { const s = [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }]; addBackupShift(s, { id: 3 }); return s.length === 2; })()

cases.name: result appended
cases.check: (() => { const s = [{ id: 1 }]; const r = addBackupShift(s, { id: 9 }); return r.length === 2 && r[0].id === 1 && r[1].id === 9; })()

cases.name: new array returned
cases.check: (() => { const s = []; const r = addBackupShift(s, { id: 1 }); return r !== s && s.length === 0; })()

reviewed_explanation.text: Line 2 makes updated point to the same array as schedule, so push on line 3 changes the original. Copying first — [...schedule] (option a) or schedule.slice() (option b) — fixes it. Freezing (option c) makes push throw a TypeError. Copying on return (option d) is too late: the original was already modified on line 3. Note that both copies are shallow; the shift objects themselves are shared, which is fine here because they are not changed.
reviewed_explanation.accepted_summary: Line 2 with fix a or fix b.

review.notes: Patch outcomes confirmed by running reviewed cases.
